styles.label: Culture
styles.blurb: Nike Art Gallery, Freedom Park and the music scene.

styles.label: Food
styles.blurb: Jollof, suya and smoky party rice across the city.

styles.label: Beaches
styles.blurb: Atlantic sand at Tarkwa Bay and Landmark.

stays.why: Central for business, restaurants and the Landmark beach; easy to reach Ikoyi and Lagos Island.
Quiet, leafy and upscale; close to the museums and good restaurants. Good for couples and business.
Beach clubs, nightlife and many mid-range stays. Traffic can be heavy; pick a place near your plans.
Near the airport and quieter at night. Cheaper, but far from the beaches and island sights.

food: Try Nigerian classics: jollof rice, egusi soup with pounded yam, and pepper soup. Portions are big.
Suya (grilled spiced beef skewers) is a street favourite; buy from busy stalls in the evening.
Lagos does great seafood: grilled fish, prawns and catfish pepper soup near the water.
Cheap eats: buka (local canteens) serve rice and stew for a few hundred naira; check prices on the day.
Street food and tap water are risky for some stomachs. Drink bottled water and eat where it is busy and freshly cooked.
more_time: Add a day for Badagry: old slave-trade sites and the coast, a long drive west of the city.
Take a short boat trip to Tarkwa Bay or a Lekki beach for a slower day by the Atlantic.
Music fans can spend an evening at a live afrobeats or highlife venue; ask your hotel for a safe, current recommendation.

recommend.why: Two nights covers the markets, museums and a beach day, with an evening for the music and food scene.

month_notes: January: dry and warm, about 32°C by day. One of the best months to visit.
February: warm and fairly dry, around 8 rain days. Good for sightseeing.
March: rain picks up to about 16 days. Carry a light rain jacket.
April: similar to March, warm and wet at times. Plan indoor backups.
May: wet season starts in earnest, about 22 rain days. Expect short heavy downpours.
June: the wettest month, around 28 rain days. Pack rain gear and keep plans flexible.
July: still very wet and cooler, highs near 27°C. Good for indoor culture and food.
August: wet, about 22 rain days. Some dry breaks; check forecasts daily.
September: very wet again, around 27 rain days. Flooding can slow traffic.
October: still rainy, about 27 days. Roads can flood; allow extra time.
November: rain eases to about 18 days. A good shoulder month.
December: dry and warm, around 6 rain days. A top month for beaches and nights out.

climate_guide.summary: Tropical climate: hot all year, with a long wet season from roughly April to October and a drier stretch from November to March.

items.title: Best time: December to February
items.text: Warm days around 32°C and the fewest rain days (5–8). Ideal for beaches, markets and walking.

items.title: Wet season: April to October
items.text: Rain days climb to 22–28 a month. Downpours are often short but heavy; carry a rain jacket.

items.title: Hot and humid all year
items.text: Highs stay between 27 and 32°C, lows near 24–26°C. Humidity makes it feel hotter.

items.title: Flooding slows traffic
items.text: In the wettest months (June, September, October) roads can flood. Allow extra time and avoid low-lying routes.

items.title: Beach days need timing
items.text: Beaches are best in the dry months. In the wet season, go early and check the sky.

items.title: What to pack
items.text: Light breathable clothes, sandals, sunscreen, a rain jacket and insect repellent. A light layer for air-conditioned rooms.

transit.best: Ride apps (Uber, Bolt) for most trips; BRT buses and the Blue Line rail if you're saving money.

modes.text: Blue Line rail runs Marina to Mile 2; fare about ₦375, Cowry Card only.
BRT buses use dedicated lanes; cash not accepted, buy a Cowry Card (₦500–1,000).
Uber and Bolt work widely; taxis are metered or negotiated. Agree the price first.
Not recommended for first-time visitors; traffic is heavy and driving rules are loosely followed.
Only in a few central areas. The city is spread out and pavements are uneven.
Yellow minibuses cover most routes; fares start around ₦50 and rise with distance. Cash only.
Quick but risky, and banned in many districts and after dark. Avoid unless you know the area.
Ferries link Lagos Island, Banana Island, Mile 2 and the mainland. A fast way to skip traffic.
